newsitem.title: UK: Weaker Brent paper curve pulls North Sea lower.
newsitem.headline: Weaker Brent paper curve pulls North Sea lower.

text.p: Weaker Brent paper spreads pulled North Sea crudes lower on Thursday as an overhang of prompt barrels continued to weigh on the market, traders said.
At $22.30 a barrel, outright Dec Brent paper was about 15 cents firmer but the Nov/Dec contango continued to deepen and other spreads were also weaker.
Dec/Jan was pegged at +26 cents after trading early at +32 cents. Jan/Feb traded at +42 cents but slipped by midafternoon to talk at +38/+43 cents, dealers said.
Most activity was concentrated in Brent CFDs, with next week's dates fetching Jan -12 cents, equivalent to Dec -40/-42.
They were later talked at -50/-41 cents, with the following week at Jan -9/-7 cents, dealers said.

Dated Brent was little moved, with two Nov 15-17 cargoes offered at Dec Brent -50 cents after trade at Dec -57 cents for a cargo loading a day earlier. Two more Brents were due to turn wet on Thursday, including a deferred Nov 21-23 loader.
"We definitely have an overhang but it is difficult to value Brent when you have people with big CFD positions," said an oil company trader.
The first two weeks of December saw active trade with Dec 2-6/9-13 rolls trading twice at +3 cents and one at +2 cents.
In the Mediterranean, the sour crude market was steady with Russian Urals seen holding onto recent gains after trading Wednesday at Dated Brent -86 cents cif Med up from Tuesday's -93/-95 cents.
Wednesday's level was heard repeated to the same buyer, a trade house, on Thursday but details could not be immediately confirmed.
Having bought up Nigerian grades at the peak of gas oil's rally, Med refiners were now looking to switch to sours.
"The only thing holding them back is a lack of ullage," said one. --Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
